description: The line plot illustrates the performance of various pre-trained models on the multi-document summarization (MDS) task, measured by the overall ROUGE-G score—defined as the geometric mean of ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, and ROUGE-L—aggregated across six MDS benchmarks. The x-axis represents the number of training examples, with values at 0, 16, and 64, indicating low-shot settings. The y-axis shows the ROUGE-G score, ranging from 11.0 to 19.0. The plot compares several models: PELMS (solid green line), PELMS (5%) (dashed green line), Primera (solid red line), Primera (5%) (dashed red line), Pegasus-X (solid blue line), Pegasus-X (5%) (dashed blue line), Centrum (solid yellow line), and Centrum (5%) (dashed yellow line). At 0 training examples, PELMS achieves a score of approximately 16.5, while Pegasus-X starts at around 13.5. As the number of training examples increases to 64, PELMS reaches a score of about 18.5, and Pegasus-X reaches approximately 14.5. All models show improved performance with more training data, with PELMS consistently outperforming the other models across all data quantities and both training methods (fully-supervised and adapter training). The dashed lines, representing adapter training with only 5% of parameters tuned, generally show lower performance than their solid counterparts, indicating that full parameter tuning yields better results. However, even with limited parameter updates, PELMS maintains a competitive edge over the other models.
